_comment: Hand-maintained, sourced findings the automatic sources can't see (a framework author who never published a release for the current game version; breakage reported only in Steam Workshop comments). Applied by status_logic.apply_hand_checks: a check only ever LOWERS a framework's verdict, and only while the game's current patch label equals patch_label (or its series equals patch_series) AND the framework has published nothing newer than release_at_check. So it expires by itself on the next game patch or the framework's next release. Every entry needs checked (date), text (shown on the page) and sources.

skyrim-se.text: The newest official Engine Fixes release (7.0.21-beta5, Aug 23) predates 1.7.104. The author committed a "1.7.104 build" on Aug 29 but hasn't published a release; players asked for one (issues #103 and #105) and many use an unofficial fork (kxgcayh 7.0.23) instead. Mods that require Engine Fixes, such as Community Shaders, need that fork or a downgrade to 1.7.99 until an official release.

europa-universalis-v.text: Since 1.4 went live, Workshop comments from many players report CMF crashing saves to desktop, hiding the laws tab and causing multiplayer checksum mismatches, and a Nov 18 comment says the Workshop download is still CMF 2.4.1 with metadata for EU5 1.3.*. It hasn't updated since Oct 3 and its GitHub shows no 1.4 work (last commit Aug 19). Leave CMF, and mods that require it, off for 1.4 until it updates.

total-war-warhammer-3.text: Since Patch 9.0.5 (Nov 3), at least seven players have reported in Workshop comments (Nov 7-19, in English, Chinese and Russian) that Mod Configuration Tool resets every mod's settings to defaults after a manual battle or loading a save. MCT hasn't updated since Jul 19. Mods configured through MCT may quietly run on default settings until it updates.
